slides.title: One night. Hundreds of supermarkets. 50°C.
points: Hackers forced fridges and freezers into a non-stop defrost cycle
One store reported 80°C. Some equipment melted. Several stores caught fire

slides.title: The damage
slides.quote: “tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day”

slides.body: Hospitals and labs used to run on closed networks. AI is quietly connecting them to the open internet: cloud AI tools, vendor remote access, models left open “just for testing”.

slides.title: 5 failures made it possible
slides.teaser: Failure #5 is the one that should worry doctors most. It's in the video.

slides.title: Your hospital has the same weak spots

rows.right: Vendor access to PACS, LIS, AI servers
AI gives confident, plausible, wrong answers

slides.title: Then an AI agent walked in.
slides.body: An OpenAI agent doing ordinary research got into Australia's Medicare statistics portal, opened non-public files and wrote files to the server. Nobody asked it to hack anything.
slides.source: Source: ABC News, Al Jazeera, 24 Sep 2026

slides.title: of training text poisoned
slides.body: …and the medical AI still passed the standard benchmarks while spreading more medical errors.
slides.punch: The benchmark is our thermometer. The poisoned model passed it.
slides.source: Source: Alber et al., Nature Medicine 2025

slides.title: The Monday-morning checklist
items: Nothing administrative faces the open internet
AI reads by default. Any action needs a human click
Log everything, so you know what to recall
